problem: Event-based vision work focuses on perception (odometry, flow, SLAM, detection); there is no real-world dataset pairing raw event streams with expert action labels for indoor navigation, and no end-to-end imitation policy trained on real RGB-Event data, especially for low-light where RGB fails.
motivation: Indoor service robots face motion blur, dim lighting and high dynamic range, which degrade frame-based RGB policies. Event cameras have microsecond latency and high dynamic range, but their use for closed-loop control is underexplored because data with aligned actions is lacking.
key_idea: Build a real-world synchronized RGB-Event-action person-following dataset (eNavi) and train a late-fusion policy (frozen RGB MobileNetV3 + trainable event MobileNetV3 + transformer fusion) by behavioral cloning to test low-light robustness.
insight: Event inputs make training converge faster (early stopping at epochs ~10-37 vs RGB running all 50) and give lower validation MAE (e.g. Multi-Path Mixed-Light: Fusion 0.0370 vs RGB 0.0707). In zero-shot low light after Normal-Light-only training, RGB is fine on simple single-path data (0.0210 to 0.0213), but on multi-path data Fusion achieves the lowest low-light MAE (0.0467 vs RGB 0.0514). The benefit is therefore modest and appears mainly for complex trajectories; the evidence is offline action-prediction error only.
method: Hardware/data collection: TurtleBot 2 with Jetson Orin Nano, Prophesee EVK4 event camera (1280x720) and Blackfly S RGB camera on a beam splitter, hardware-triggered at 30 Hz by an STM32; homography calibration with a blinking checkerboard; ~2 h, 175+ episodes, 3 indoor maps, 2 subjects, normal and low light
Synchronization pipeline: RGB timestamps as anchors; events in (t_{i-1}, t_i] accumulated into a 2-channel polarity histogram; commands averaged over the same window; stored as HDF5 tuples (I, E, a)
Odometry-based action labels: ground-truth linear/angular velocity from wheel-odometry twists (averaged per frame window) rather than noisy joystick commands
ENP encoders: pretrained frozen MobileNetV3-Small for RGB (320x180x3) and trainable MobileNetV3-Small for events (320x180x2)
Fusion + head: the two feature tokens go to a Transformer encoder block, then an MLP predicts (v, w)
Training: behavioral cloning with L1 loss, AdamW lr 2e-4, wd 3e-4, batch 64, 80/10/10 split, 50 epochs with early stopping (patience 8)
12 variants: {RGB, Event, Fusion} x {Single-Path, Multi-Path} x {Normal-Light, Mixed-Light}

setting.backbone: Dual MobileNetV3-Small (RGB pretrained/frozen, event trainable) + Transformer encoder fusion + MLP head
setting.training_data: eNavi: ~2 h, 175+ real episodes of person-following teleoperation; single map for in-distribution train/test
setting.observation: RGB frames + event frames (2-channel polarity histogram), 320x180
setting.action_space: continuous differential-drive velocities (linear v, angular w)
setting.simulator: real world only (offline evaluation on held-out dataset trajectories)
setting.privileged: none at test; training labels derived from wheel odometry

numbers.extra: trained on Normal-Light only; metric is action MAE (lower is better), open-loop

numbers_note: Custom dataset; offline action-prediction MAE only, no closed-loop navigation success metrics. The multi-path low-light trajectory figure reports linear MAE 0.125 and angular MAE 0.078 for one sample trajectory (not tabulated).
results: Event-containing policies converge faster and reach lower validation MAE than RGB (Multi-Path Mixed-Light: Fusion 0.0370 vs RGB 0.0707). Zero-shot to low light with multi-path training, Fusion gets Total MAE 0.0467 vs RGB 0.0514 and YOLOv8n+PID 0.1033; on single-path data RGB is as good or better (0.0213 vs Fusion 0.0222).
limitations: Evaluation is open-loop action MAE on held-out dataset trajectories; no closed-loop or real-robot deployment results
Time-synchronized fusion is costly for real-time edge inference; RGB-only or Event-only are more practical
Small dataset (~2 h, 3 maps, 2 subjects); event-only sometimes beats fusion and the low-light gains are modest/mixed
